findings.summary: The refusal test does not first show that the same writer, in the same repo, accepts a legitimate append. The behavior-evidence default asks for that.
findings.evidence: The plan appends the builder's record, then asserts Refused for a changed record. The behavior-evidence default asks a denial test to first show the action succeeding without the protection. Fix: In the same test, show that appending a record at a new path succeeds (the tip moves). Then show that appending changed bytes at legacy-exempt.json is refused, with the tip and blob unchanged.

findings.summary: Dropping the NoIntent finding whenever a cutover is given changes the part 1 rule for post-C0 commits, which is out of scope.
findings.evidence: Out of scope: 'Changing the part 1 records-only rule for post-C0 commits'. The plan says 'The plan skips it.' Fix: Keep part 1's behavior for post-C0 commits: if there are post-C0 commits and no intents, emit the same finding part 1 would. Skip it only when there are no post-C0 commits at all, and test that case.
findings.location: Open questions, item 3 (NoIntent with a cutover)

findings.summary: Copying the athena.toml comments word for word would put a person's name into a record and into code.
findings.evidence: athena.toml:152-154, in the 02837e0 comment, names the user ('with Sri's approval of 2026-10-23'). Fix: Write the reasons in neutral terms, for example 'approved by the owner on 2026-10-23 (BRIEF.md addendum)', and leave out personal names.

findings.summary: 49c6ac1 has no comment of its own, so its reason must come from the section header (athena.toml:136-137, commits that predate Athena).
findings.evidence: athena.toml has comment lines for 64ecdc9, ee4b0dd, f2a8453, 5a73478, 39962ed and 02837e0, but none for 49c6ac1. Fix: Use the header text ('predates Athena; exempt from the governed-content invariant, design §7.3') as its reason, and say so in a doc comment.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot, and what it relies on exists. check_history(git, tip) is in crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs:27, and HistoryState.exempt is set once, from tip_config.history.exempt (line 50-52). invariant::is_exempt reads that state (invariant.rs:90-98). So an override that replaces only that list reuses the logic without copying it, which is what criterion 6 asks. LegacyExempt and LegacyExemptEntry exist in athena-data history.rs, along with the athena.legacy-exempt/1 schema and a validate method. RecordsWriter already returns RecordsError::Refused (records_branch.rs:162, 457). builtin_config comes from include_str!("../../../athena.toml") (lib.rs:32), and its exempt list holds exactly the seven requested ids (athena.toml:156). That makes the criterion 4 demonstration sound. Each demonstration checks an outcome (excused versus failing, refused rewrite, post-C0 versus at-C0 verdicts) and would fail without the behavior. There are no athena.toml field changes, and the work fits one producer run. I have three minor points: the append-only test should first show that a legitimate append succeeds; skipping NoIntent when a cutover is given is a quiet change to the part 1 rule; and copying the athena.toml comments word for word would carry a person's name into a record.
